summary:
Socratic.Trade's peer-serving surface (merged via PR #2314, present on origin/main but NOT in the stale local checkout, which is 42 commits behind) consists of two bearer-gated read routes: GET /api/market/prices/{symbol} and GET /api/market/spx (served as SPY bars). Both authenticate with the same APP_B_INGEST_TOKEN shared secret as the import receiver via constant-time verifySecuritiesImportToken; middleware passes bearer requests through unauthenticated for exactly those two paths, and validation happens in the route handler. Responses use the shared-package PriceSeries / {closes} envelopes with closes DESCENDING, always-200 when authorized (unknown symbol or empty range returns empty closes so Congress.Trade only falls back on non-200). from/to are inclusive YYYY-MM-DD; an omitted from defaults to ~366 days back; there is no cap on range width, no pagination, and no rate limiting anywhere on these routes.

Critically, the routes do NOT serve from a local price table. They call fetchDailyOHLC — the app's live daily-OHLC cascade: (1) local imported-EOD DB tier, which is DEFAULT OFF (SECURITIES_IMPORT_HISTORY_TIER_ENABLED unset → skipped) and density-guarded (≥200 bars); (2) an HTTP call BACK to Congress.Trade (gated by CONGRESS_TRADE_READS_ENABLED); (3) Massive REST (metered by a per-minute reservation, 100/min default, 5/min if free-tier detected); then Tradier → Marketstack → Yahoo (only 1y of data) → Stooq. Results are cached in-process for ~30 minutes per symbol. So on every cache miss, serving a Congress.Trade request consumes Socratic's Massive/vendor quota, and when the App A tier is enabled it fires a guaranteed-wasted echo call back to Congress.Trade (CT's /api/market/prices is D1-read-only, so the loop is bounded at one hop, but CT asked precisely because it lacks the data).

The 5y flat-file store (data/history-5y, 3,334 files, 538MB) is a dev-only, one-shot artifact: written by scripts/hoard-5y-universe.ts (which skips any existing non-empty file, so re-runs never refresh), last written 2026-07-24 with newest bars 2026-07-24, not in git, not in the Docker image, and absent from the prod volume — the rollout note for PR #2314 explicitly decided against serving from it. No code under src/lib reads history-5y at all, and nothing ingests it into Socratic's DB. Socratic's only persistent price store is imported_price_eod/imported_spx_eod/imported_securities_ref, populated solely by Congress.Trade's return-path pushes to POST /api/admin/securities/import — and the read tier over that store is default OFF. Daily freshness flows the OTHER way: a scheduler-invoked once-per-UTC-day congress-share batch (gated on CONGRESS_TRADE_TOKEN + CONGRESS_SHARE_ENABLED) pushes SPX + up to 2,000 tickers × ~260 closes to Congress.Trade, draining up to 500 tickers/night from CT's /api/export/price-needs. Coverage-wise, the flat-file universe (S&P500+Nasdaq100+Dow30+Russell2000+S&P100+ETFs/REITs ≈ 3,334 tickers) is an index universe, not CT's 4,152 traded-ticker universe — the residual ~10,961 anchor-less trades skew toward delisted/micro-cap symbols outside it, exactly the symbols where Socratic's cascade will fan out to vendors (and often still miss). Whether the relevant prod flags (SECURITIES_IMPORT_HISTORY_TIER_ENABLED, CONGRESS_TRADE_READS_ENABLED, CONGRESS_SHARE_ENABLED) are actually enabled in Infisical is not determinable from the repos.

Flat-file universe = index membership (S&P500+Nasdaq100+Dow30+Russell2000+S&P100+major ETFs/REITs, scripts/hoard-5y-universe.ts:60-85) ≈ 3,334 tickers vs CT's 4,152 traded tickers — the ~10,961 anchor-less CT trades skew to symbols OUTSIDE this universe (the in-universe ones were already backfilled into CT per the 2026-07-31 rollout), so peer reads for them will usually fan out to Massive and often still return empty

gaps.title: Peer reads are not local-first: every cache-miss burns Socratic vendor quota
gaps.detail: The 'primary price source' routes serve from the live fetchDailyOHLC cascade with only a ~30-min in-process cache (origin/main:src/lib/market-read.ts:71,92; history.ts:20). The one local-DB tier is default OFF (history.ts:395-397,414) and its store (imported_price_eod) only contains what CT itself pushed back. So a CT catch-up sweep over thousands of tickers = thousands of Massive REST calls (metered at 100/min, massive.ts:44,88-96), plus Tradier/Marketstack/Yahoo/Stooq fallthrough — the opposite of the owner's 'ST handles the cascade, CT reads cheap local data' intent.
gaps.fixSketch: Give Socratic a real local EOD store and serve peer reads DB-first: (a) write-through — persist every cascade result into a price_eod table keyed (ticker,date); (b) a nightly append job using ONE Massive grouped-daily call for the whole market (fetchGroupedBarsRest already exists, massive.ts:110+) to keep it current; (c) have the /api/market routes read that table first and only cascade on genuine gaps. Alternatively, as a stopgap, set SECURITIES_IMPORT_HISTORY_TIER_ENABLED=on in prod so CT's pushed-back closes at least short-circuit repeats.

gaps.title: No bulk/multi-symbol endpoint for CT's ~10,961-anchor backfill
gaps.detail: CT's peer client pulls strictly one symbol per HTTP request (/Users/jay/Code/Congress.Trade/app/src/prices/peer.ts:33-45); the shared CongressTradeClient has no multi-ticker price call either (congress-trading-shared/src/client.ts:226-241). Draining ~10,961 missing anchors across ~4k tickers means ~4k+ sequential requests, each a potential ST-side vendor call. Meanwhile ST already has a one-call whole-market source (grouped-daily REST) and a session-gated /api/market/flatfile route (origin/main:app/api/market/flatfile/route.ts) that peers cannot use.
gaps.fixSketch: Add a bearer-gated bulk read on ST: either GET /api/market/prices?symbols=A,B,C&from=&to= (chunked, DB-first per the fix above) or a grouped-by-date endpoint (extend /api/market/flatfile to accept the APP_B_INGEST_TOKEN bearer like the other two routes — one middleware else-if + verifySecuritiesImportToken). CT then backfills by DATE (one call per trading day) instead of by ticker: ~1,250 calls total for 5y instead of ~4k per-symbol pulls, and zero per-symbol vendor fan-out.

gaps.title: CT→ST→CT echo hop wastes a call on every peer-originated miss
gaps.detail: When CONGRESS_TRADE_READS_ENABLED is on, ST's cascade tier 2 calls Congress.Trade back for the very symbol CT just asked ST about (origin/main:src/lib/history.ts:96,377). CT's route is D1-only (rest.ts:690-713) so recursion is bounded, but for peer-originated requests the hop is guaranteed-useless (CT asked because its D1 lacks the data) or worse — it can return CT's own partial series back to CT, masking a fresher Massive pull that the next tier would have provided.
gaps.fixSketch: Skip the App A tier for peer-originated requests: the market-read routes pass an option (e.g. fetchDailyOHLC(symbol, now, undefined, { skipAppATier: true }) or a dedicated fetcher) so the cascade goes imported-tier → Massive directly. One-line plumb through market-read.ts's injectable fetcher.

gaps.title: No rate limit on the token-gated peer read routes
gaps.detail: Middleware only forwards bearer requests (origin/main:middleware.ts:378-385) and the handlers only check the token — there is no per-minute cap, unlike admin routes which get admin-operation-guard limits (origin/main:src/lib/admin-operation-guard.ts:38). A CT retry storm, a misconfigured loop, or a leaked APP_B_INGEST_TOKEN can drive unbounded cascade fan-out (each miss = up to 6 upstream fetches) and saturate the single Coolify Node process. Massive's own reservation only protects Massive, not Tradier/Yahoo/Stooq or ST's CPU.
gaps.fixSketch: Add a cheap token-scoped sliding-window limiter in the two handlers (same in-process timestamp-array pattern as reserveMassiveRestCall, e.g. 300 req/min) returning 429 with Retry-After; CT already has 429 retry resilience from the 2026-07-31 rollout, so it degrades gracefully.

gaps.title: 5y flat-file store is stale, orphaned, and lives only on the laptop
gaps.detail: data/history-5y: 3,334 files, frozen at 2026-07-24 (verified mtimes + newest bars), written once by scripts/hoard-5y-universe.ts whose skip-if-exists guard (lines 25-29) means re-runs never refresh existing tickers; nothing in src/lib reads it, it is not in git/Docker/prod (docs/rollouts/2026-07-31-market-read-routes.md §3). The '5 years of Massive flat files' asset the fleet reasons about is effectively a one-shot local download that decays daily and cannot serve production.
gaps.fixSketch: Decide its role explicitly: (a) promote — ingest it once into the new ST price_eod table (local script → POST or direct sqlite load) and keep it current with the nightly grouped-daily append, then delete the JSON dir; or (b) demote — document it as the consumed one-off source of CT's 2M-close backfill and remove it. Also fix the hoard script to refresh (append bars newer than the file's last bar) if it is kept.

gaps.title: Series-depth blindness: shallow tiers can poison the cache and deep history (pre-2021) is unserveable
gaps.detail: The cascade takes the FIRST source with ≥2 bars (history.ts:117-126): if Massive/Tradier miss and Yahoo answers, only ~1y of bars (history.ts:272) is cached for 30 min and served for ANY requested range — a CT deep-history request (from=2021) then gets a truncated or empty-closes 200 and CT treats ST as authoritative-empty, falling back to metered vendors. Even at best the cascade starts at now−1825d (history.ts:82) and the flat files start 2021-01-01, so CT trades older than ~5y can never be anchored via ST.
gaps.fixSketch: Track per-series earliest-bar date; when a request's `from` predates the cached/fetched series start, bypass shallow tiers (Yahoo) and retry deeper sources, or include a seriesStart field in the response envelope so CT can distinguish 'no data' from 'window not covered' (shared-schema addition, backward-compatible optional field).

gaps.title: No peer-readable company-ref/enrichment endpoint while CT still burns ~283 FMP calls/day on 403s
gaps.detail: ST exposes no bearer-gated GET for refs/fundamentals (only nightly pushes ST→CT and CT-facing pulls FROM CT); CT's enrichment still calls the suspended FMP account (~283 wasted calls/day per the 2026-07-31 rollout context). CT already has securities_ref rows from ST's nightly ref pushes, so most metadata demand is satisfiable without any vendor.
gaps.fixSketch: Primary fix is CT-side: disable/hard-skip the FMP enrichment client while the account is 403-suspended (its fatal-error classifier already recognizes 401/402/403 — /Users/jay/Code/Congress.Trade/app/src/prices/service.ts:135) and lean on ST's nightly ref pushes. Optionally add bearer-gated GET /api/market/refs?tickers= on ST (reads imported_securities_ref + screener cache) for on-demand gap-fill.

gaps.title: Prod flag state undetermined — the whole cache-aside design may be dormant
gaps.detail: SECURITIES_IMPORT_HISTORY_TIER_ENABLED, CONGRESS_TRADE_READS_ENABLED, and CONGRESS_SHARE_ENABLED all default off in code, and the last repo evidence (origin/main:docs/EFFORT-LOG.md:1357, 2026-07-13) says activation was 'Awaiting owner action in Infisical'. If CONGRESS_SHARE_ENABLED is off, the nightly needs-drain that should be erasing the 10,961-anchor backlog is not running at all.
gaps.fixSketch: Verify the three flags in the Infisical/Coolify env for socratictrade.com (owner or an agent with env access); record the confirmed state in STATUS.md; enable CONGRESS_SHARE_ENABLED + the imported-history tier if the owner's ST-as-cascade direction stands.

gaps.title: Local Socratic checkout 42 commits behind — audits and local dev see a pre-#2314 world
gaps.detail: /Users/jay/Code/Socratic.Trade main is behind origin/main by 42 commits; the peer routes, market-read.ts, and the rollout doc do not exist in the working tree (verified: find under app/api/market shows only flatfile/route.ts locally). summary:
Congress.Trade's outbound market-data surfaces (all routed through trackedFetch per app/docs/third-party-usage-telemetry.md:72-88) split into three groups. (1) The PRICE CHAIN is already rerouted per the 2026-07-31 rollout: prices/service.ts:118-124 builds peer-first (SocraticTrade GET /api/market/prices/{symbol} and /api/market/spx with the APP_B_INGEST_TOKEN bearer, prices/peer.ts:20-60) falling back to Massive aggregates (SPX served as SPY, prices/massive.ts:72), with PRICE_PROVIDER=massive confirmed in prod. (2) COMPANY-PROFILE ENRICHMENT is the remaining direct-vendor hot spot: enrichment/service.ts:185-199 builds a chain FMP -> Massive -> Intrinio -> TwelveData -> Finnhub -> Tiingo -> SEC EDGAR, run from two Deno cron lanes (daily-market-data at :07 and hourly-enrichment at :47, src/deno/cronLanes.ts:44-58). FMP (enrichment/fmp.ts:76-83, /stable/profile) is the only budgeted provider and fetches companyName, sector, industry, marketCap, sharesOutstanding (derived), country, state, exchange, currency, ipoDate, CIK, ETF/ADR flags (fmp.ts:29-64). The FMP account is suspended (every call 403s), yet the key remains configured, so every enrichment candidate burns one dead FMP call first (~283/day per docs/rollouts/2026-07-31-price-pipeline-flatfiles-socratic-primary.md:65-68); worse, because hasFmp=true makes the run's candidate selection budget-bounded (service.ts:309-315, early-return at :330), the dead key can throttle or fully halt even the healthy Massive/EDGAR enrichment once the daily counter fills with 403s. (3) CONGRESS-SPECIFIC feeds are not reroutable: House Clerk (incl. proxy.cors.sh fallback, ingestion/houseSource.ts:360), Senate eFD, OGE, house-stock-watcher S3 seed (backfill/seed.ts:96), unitedstates.github.io legislators/photos (admin/routes.ts:991-992,1075), Quiver and Unusual Whales disclosure probes (ingestion/tradeLatency.ts:705-748), the FMP house/senate-latest disclosure-latency probe (tradeLatency.ts:676-703, throttled to one run per 300s = up to ~576 FMP calls/day when DISCLOSURE_LATENCY_WATCH_ENABLED, :1577-1586), and the admin-triggered FMP senate-history recovery (backfill/fmpSenateRecovery.ts:309, invoked at admin/routes.ts:4227). The FMP-based ones among these are dead weight while the key is suspended but their replacement is a different vendor decision (Quiver/UW), not a Socratic reroute.

On the Socratic side, the reroute raw material for enrichment already exists. Socratic's keyless Nasdaq screener pulls the full ~8,000-symbol US universe with companyName, sector, industry and marketCap in one call (src/lib/market.ts:88, row mapping :910-914), supplemented by keyless Nasdaq quote/summary and Yahoo enrichment (src/lib/data-providers.ts:1040-1043, 2340-2488). Socratic ALREADY pushes partial company refs (name/sector/industry/marketCap only, src/lib/congress-share.ts:239-256) to Congress.Trade's idempotent import receiver — but only for symbols its own scans touch, throttled 6h (congress-share.ts:588-627); the nightly batch pushes closes+SPX, not refs (congress-share.ts:652-760). Congress.Trade's receiver (POST /api/admin/securities/import, admin/routes.ts:~7950-8290) and its non-destructive ref upsert (enrichment/service.ts:460-506) can absorb bulk ref pushes today with zero new code. What Socratic CANNOT supply: CIK, exchange, state-of-incorporation, IPO date — but SEC EDGAR (free, dedicated pacer, enrichment/sec.ts) and Massive's reference endpoint (unmetered, enrichment/providers.ts:73-84) already cover those in the existing chain, so dropping FMP loses essentially nothing. The Massive flat files are OHLCV bars only (v/vw/o/c/h/l/t/n — verified against data/history-5y/AAPL.json) and hold no company metadata, so the reroute must come from the screener/quote path or Socratic DB, not the flat files. Remaining minor surfaces: logo.dev + GitHub ticker-logo proxy (ui/tickerLogos.ts:95-123) is edge-cached a week and cheap — leave direct; SEC EDGAR enrichment is free/public-domain — leave direct.

summary:
The intended architecture in Socratic.Trade's docs is a bidirectional "fetch once at the cheapest source, share so neither double-pays" design (docs/congress-trade-data-plan.md): App B (Socratic) is the market-data provider — after-scan refs push + nightly chunked bulk push of prices/SPX/insider/short-volume to App A's idempotent POST /api/admin/securities/import, plus an on-demand fullHistory backfill — while App A (Congress.Trade) is the congressional authority, feeding App B via public /api/transactions pulls, /api/analytics/* overlays, a webhook (POST /api/webhooks/congress), and a subscription-authenticated SSE stream (/api/stream). A separate durable-principles doc (data-architecture-push-vs-poll.md) says push beats poll for discrete events, and explicitly warns that rebroadcasting raw vendor data to others is a ToS/licensing issue while relaying one's own derived events is fine.

What is actually implemented diverges on the money path. The documented Socratic->Congress nightly bulk PUSH is fully built but default-OFF and still off per the enablement backlog (CONGRESS_SHARE_ENABLED=off, FEATURE-ENABLEMENT-BACKLOG.md:87; data-plan §7's "Enable in prod" checkbox is unchecked). Instead, after the FMP suspension, the 2026-07-31 rollout made Congress.Trade PULL from Socratic per-symbol: a peer PriceClient (app/src/prices/peer.ts) issues one GET /api/market/prices/{symbol} per ticker (budget up to ~5,000/day) as the PRIMARY source ahead of Massive, against new token-gated App B routes (Socratic PR #2314) that serve bars from the live fetchDailyOHLC cascade — whose first keyed provider is the SAME shared Massive key. So on App B cache misses the per-symbol poll adds an HTTP hop without conserving the shared Massive quota; the 538MB flat-file archive is dev-only and not in the prod image (2026-07-31-market-read-routes.md, Decisions). APP_B_IMPORT_URL flows App A -> App B: it is App B's import-receiver URL used by App A's live share-back push (share/outbound.ts), and its .origin is ALSO reused as the base for the peer READ client — an overloaded name. Both the pull and the share-back are live in prod (bearer + URL confirmed in the CT rollout).

On licensing: the docs prescribe a per-provider ToS review and allowlist before sharing vendor data (chat-multiuser-learning-design.md:145) and state plainly that rebroadcasting raw vendor data is not fine (data-architecture-push-vs-poll.md:52-54), but the referenced "market-data sharing guardrails" doc (rollouts/2026-06-19-market-data-sharing-guardrails.md) only governs cross-USER sharing inside Socratic, not cross-app vendor redistribution. No Massive ToS review is recorded anywhere, and Congress.Trade re-serves the Massive-derived closes on PUBLIC no-auth routes (/market/prices, /market/spx in app/src/delivery/rest.ts) — so compliance of the new SocraticTrade-primary chain is undetermined, with the docs' own stated principle in tension with it. On Usage-Monitor: nothing in any doc has it coordinating the shared Massive key between apps. It receives call-volume telemetry from both apps, serves monthly-USD /api/budget-status (Socratic budget enforcement default-off; Congress's monitorBudgetGate is advisory and discretionary-lane-only), and holds the Massive subscription's knobEnv (MASSIVE_REST_MAX_CALLS_PER_MINUTE=100) as machine-readable data — but the consumer sync was explicitly out of scope and no cross-app rate-window arbitration exists; Congress.Trade's own code attributes its Massive 429s to "a shared key saturated by sibling apps" and handles them locally with retry/backoff.

Congress.Trade's price chain is a peer-first fallback stack assembled per refresh run in `pricePlan()` (app/src/prices/service.ts:99-125): when APP_B_IMPORT_URL is set, a SocraticTrade peer client (peer.ts) is wrapped as the PRIMARY leg of `buildFallbackPriceClient(peer, base)`, and the single base vendor is chosen by PRICE_PROVIDER — 'massive' in Infisical prod per the 2026-07-31 rollout doc — so the live order is SocraticTrade -> Massive, with FMP/Tiingo only reachable via other PRICE_PROVIDER values or the keyless fallback order FMP->Massive->Tiingo. The peer is consulted first on every call (one spxHistory per run, one eodHistory per selected ticker); the vendor runs only when the peer returns non-200, throws, or returns an empty closes array (fallback.ts:13-35). The daily driver is the Deno cron lane 'daily-market-data' ('7 * * * *', once per UTC day via KV date stamp, cronLanes.ts:43-47 + jobs.ts:258-259), which runs enrichment then runPriceRefresh, then pushes the run's delta back to SocraticTrade via shareWithPeer (share/outbound.ts). Selection is FIFO oldest-traded-first, bounded by a per-run budget = FMP_DAILY_CALL_CAP (5,000 in prod, unmetered when provider is massive), fresh-through the last completed ET trading session (service.ts:213-220, 262-292).

Unpriceable tickers are handled by a two-stage negative cache in securities_ref.price_unavailable: a first confirmed-empty result (both peer AND vendor say no data — vendor 404s map to [] while auth/5xx/429 throw and skip without marking) sets stage 1 with a 7-day recheck; a second consecutive miss escalates to stage 2 with a 30-day recheck; a successful fetch whose newest close is >14 days old sets stage 3 (STALLED, 30-day) (service.ts:36-72, 467-497, 524-548). At steady state the ~2,059 remaining unpriceable tickers cost roughly a 30-day trickle of paired peer+Massive probes and are excluded from both selection and the backfill pending count (admin/routes.ts:8881-8898). When SocraticTrade is down entirely the chain degrades cleanly — every peer error/non-200 collapses to [] and Massive serves directly — but there is no read-side circuit breaker (unlike the push path's target circuit, outbound.ts:114-121), so a dead peer costs up to ~budget wasted HTTPS round trips per run, silently. The worse failure mode is partial data: any NON-empty peer response is accepted as authoritative and the vendor is never consulted, so a stale-but-dense peer series masks Massive and, past 14 days, can wrongly negative-cache a priceable ticker for 30 days.

Telemetry has two real defects. Peer reads go through trackedFetch but without `dynamicTarget: 'peer-app'` (peer.ts:36-38, 50-52), and socratictrade.com is not in HOST_PROVIDERS (thirdPartyTelemetry.ts:172-204), so they are attributed to provider 'external-api', not 'peer-app' — only the outbound push is correctly labeled (outbound.ts:128). Worse, the Deno cron lanes never wrap lane execution in withThirdPartyTelemetry (cronLanes.ts:161-176, deno/main.ts:154-215 — the only wraps live in index.ts:328/341/425), so trackedFetch has no ALS env during internally-scheduled daily runs and every per-attempt usage event from the daily price refresh (peer, Massive, FMP) is silently dropped; only the explicit env-passing 'daily-call-limit' event survives (jobs.ts:357-374). On freshness: the lane stamps at the first hourly firing of the UTC day (00:07 UTC = ~19-20:07 ET the prior evening) and lastTradingDay() deliberately demands only the session BEFORE the just-closed one (service.ts:199-220), so a session's close typically lands in Congress.Trade ~28 hours after the bell and current_price runs 1-2 sessions behind; same-day closes are structurally unreachable under the current schedule. The Socratic side (origin/main) serves reads from its fetchDailyOHLC cascade — imported-EOD tier (DEFAULT OFF, density- but not freshness-guarded), then a circular App A read-back tier, then Massive/Tradier/Marketstack/Yahoo/Stooq — so today 'Socratic-primary' is largely a Massive proxy with a 30-minute in-process cache, and unknown junk tickers walk the entire 6-provider cascade on every Congress.Trade recheck.

gaps.title: Single-vendor fallback: Massive auth failure aborts the run even though Tiingo is configured
gaps.detail: pricePlan builds exactly one base client (service.ts:99-125); the chain is peer -> base only. A Massive 401/402/403 (or persistent 429 after retries under FMP budgeting) is classified fatal and aborts the entire run (service.ts:135-149, 392-403, 456-464) with no attempt at Tiingo, whose key exists in config (docs/config-registry.md:24). The FMP suspension already demonstrated this failure class.

gaps.title: Closes land ~28h after the bell; same-day closes are structurally unreachable
gaps.detail: The market-data lane stamps at the first hourly firing of the UTC day, 00:07 UTC = ~19-20:07 ET the PRIOR evening (cronLanes.ts:43-47, jobs.ts:258-259), and lastTradingDay() deliberately requires only the session strictly before the current ET day (service.ts:199-220). Net effect: a Thursday close is fetched at ~20:07 ET Friday, so current_price and tx_performance current returns run 1-2 sessions behind even though SocraticTrade/Massive publish EOD bars within hours of the close.
gaps.fixSketch: Either gate the daily stamp so the lane's first eligible firing is >=05:00 UTC (00:00-01:00 ET, when the just-closed session is published and the ET calendar day has rolled — freshThrough then equals the just-closed session with no lastTradingDay change), or teach lastTradingDay to count the current ET day's session as complete after ~20:00 ET. One-line schedule change vs a small date-math change plus test updates in pricesRefresh.test.ts.

gaps.title: No read-side peer circuit breaker: a SocraticTrade outage costs up to ~budget wasted round trips per run
gaps.detail: Each per-ticker peer read independently swallows its failure (peer.ts:39-44); with prod budget 5,000 and a down peer, a single daily run can attempt thousands of doomed HTTPS calls (plus telemetry events when wrapped) before each falls back to Massive. The push path already has a target circuit (outbound.ts:114-121) but the read path does not, and nothing alerts — the freshness watchdog only fires when whole-table MAX(date) goes >5 days stale (share/freshness.ts:43-44).
gaps.fixSketch: Cheapest: in-run trip-wire inside buildPeerPriceClient — after N (e.g. 5) consecutive transport-level failures, skip the peer for the remainder of the process/run and log once. Better: reuse checkTargetCircuit/recordTargetFailure from delivery/targetCircuit.ts keyed on the peer origin, matching the push path.

gaps.title: Socratic serves peer reads as a Massive proxy and walks a 6-provider cascade for junk tickers
gaps.detail: With the imported-EOD tier DEFAULT OFF (history.ts:395-398 origin/main) and only a 30-min in-process cache, every Congress.Trade peer read cascades: circular App A read-back tier (history.ts:97,372-392) then Massive (fetching ~5y of bars to answer CT's 7-day window, history.ts:83) then Tradier/Marketstack/Yahoo/Stooq. For the ~2,059 unpriceable tickers, each 7/30-day recheck makes Socratic hammer all six providers (Yahoo/Stooq rate-limit-prone) before returning closes:[]. No durable store means Socratic re-fetches the same bars across CT's staggered requests once the 30-min TTL lapses.
gaps.fixSketch: On Socratic: (a) enable the imported tier in prod WITH a freshness guard (serve only if newest imported bar >= to-minus-5-sessions, else fall through) — pairs with the CT-side stale-fallback fix; (b) add a short negative cache for symbols the full cascade failed (e.g. 24h in-process or DB), so CT rechecks stop fanning out; (c) skip the App A read-back tier for requests authenticated as App A (loop hint header) to remove the circular hop.

gaps.title: Peer-served tickers still debit the metered FMP budget when fmpBudgeted
gaps.detail: calls++/budget-- fire per attempt before the client call (service.ts:369-374, 450-452), and addDailyUsed(calls) charges the shared FMP counter (service.ts:590) even for tickers the peer served with zero FMP requests. Dormant while PRICE_PROVIDER=massive, but if FMP is reinstated as primary the peer's whole point (saving metered calls) is silently defeated and enrichment's budget floor mis-shrinks.
gaps.fixSketch: Have buildFallbackPriceClient report which leg served each call (e.g. return {closes, source}) or accept an onVendorCall callback; count only vendor-leg calls toward calls/budget in runPriceRefresh.

gaps.title: CT echoes peer-sourced closes back to Socratic; stale 'delta only' invariant
gaps.detail: result.sharePrices includes every priced ticker regardless of which leg served it (service.ts:550), so since the Socratic-primary switch the daily shareWithPeer push (jobs.ts:344-352) re-uploads data Socratic itself just served — the 'data App B sent us is never echoed back' comment at jobs.ts:342-343 is no longer true. Idempotent upserts make it harmless but it wastes bandwidth/DB writes on both sides daily.
gaps.fixSketch: Tag sharePrices entries with the serving leg (same plumbing as the budget fix above) and exclude peer-served series from the push, or drop the push for prices entirely now that reads flow the other way and keep it for spx/refs only. Update the jobs.ts comment either way.

gaps.title: runPriceRefresh ignores the lane AbortSignal; 429 backoff sleeps can eat the 10-min lane deadline
gaps.detail: maybeRunDailyMarketDataJobs threads opts.signal only into runEnrichment (jobs.ts:312-318) — runPriceRefresh(env, {maxPerMinute}) at jobs.ts:330 has no signal parameter at all (service.ts:294-296), so the lane's 10-min deadline (cronLanes.ts:69) abandons rather than cleanly stops it, and with429Retries can sleep up to ~50s per rate-limited call (retry429.ts:20-22) against a shared Massive key, shrinking effective daily throughput unpredictably.
gaps.fixSketch: Add opts.signal to runPriceRefresh, check signal.aborted at the top of the per-ticker loop (mirroring enrichment's service.ts:363 pattern), and pass the lane signal at jobs.ts:330. FIFO selection already makes interrupted runs resume correctly.

gaps.title: PRICE_PROVIDER code default is 'fmp': an Infisical outage silently reverts to the suspended metered vendor
gaps.detail: pricePlan defaults to 'fmp' when PRICE_PROVIDER is unset/unresolvable (service.ts:100), and resolveSecrets falling back to env would land on the wrangler/.prod.vars default 'fmp' (wrangler_dev.log shows PRICE_PROVIDER="fmp"). With the FMP account suspended, a config-resolution blip turns every run into an immediate FMP 403 abort (peer still first, but SPX-abort at service.ts:392-403 kills the ticker loop before the peer can serve tickers).

summary:
Congress.Trade's Usage-Monitor integration is architecturally strong but has one likely-critical runtime hole and several classification/read-back gaps on the new price-chain surfaces. The metering core (app/src/shared/thirdPartyTelemetry.ts) is well built: trackedFetch emits one request-attempt event per network attempt with success/status/latency, a rateLimited flag on HTTP 429 (line 1082), and errorType on thrown errors (lines 1087-1115); events flow through INGEST_QUEUE with a stable eventId used as the receiver idempotency key, with a failure-only R2 outbox, a KV-durable circuit breaker with a D1-leased single half-open probe, DLQ terminal-reject acks, quarantine for poison events, and an R2 drain that deletes only after the receiver accepts. The Usage-Monitor receiver (src/app/api/ingest/usage/route.ts) is idempotent (dedupe + 409 collision + duplicates counters). Docs (app/docs/third-party-usage-telemetry.md) match this code closely.

The critical problem: telemetry context is established only in the Workers-style fetch/scheduled/queue handlers via withThirdPartyTelemetry (app/src/index.ts:328,341,425), but production runs the Deno container whose Deno.cron entry points (src/deno/main.ts:154-166, src/deno/cronLanes.ts:161-166 → jobs.ts) call runScheduledTick/daily lanes directly with no wrap anywhere in the deno/ call graph. Without the AsyncLocalStorage context, trackedFetch silently emits nothing (thirdPartyTelemetry.ts:1048-1049, 1062 `if (env)`). The 2026-07-31 cron-lane-split rollout (docs/EFFORT-LOG.md:943) verified the internal lane crons registered on prod, so the daily market-data lane (peer→Massive price refresh), hourly enrichment (the FMP 403 burn), watcher, disclosure-latency probe, and durable-queue drain all likely run unmetered in production. Measured token/cost events are unaffected (recordMeasuredThirdPartyUsage takes env explicitly), which is why LLM spend still appears in the monitor. Consequently: (1) peer-app SocraticTrade calls ARE metered in code — including non-2xx and network errors — but only from HTTP-triggered contexts, and they are misclassified as provider 'external-api' because prices/peer.ts passes no dynamicTarget and socratictrade.com is not in the host map; (2) Massive/Tiingo are correctly metered per retry attempt with rate-limit flags — again only in wrapped contexts; (3) the dead-FMP enrichment 403s are metered by code (enrichment/fmp.ts:81) but the scheduled burn likely never reaches the monitor due to the cron gap, and even delivered events' status/success/rateLimited metadata is persisted but not exposed by any monitor read API (usage-events raw select omits metadata), so the waste shows only as cost-less request volume.

On read-back (question 4): yes — src/shared/monitorBudgetGate.ts polls GET /api/budget-status (fail-open, 2-min isolate cache, threshold default 1.0), documented in app/docs/config-registry.md:148-168, and the monitor serves it (Usage-Monitor src/app/api/budget-status/route.ts). But the only consumer is the extraction backlog autopilot (extraction/autopilot.ts:1036); the price chain never consults it, and budget-status is monthly-USD only, so it cannot express Massive/Tiingo per-minute quotas anyway. There is also a production auth trap: CT falls back to sending its ingest token as the read credential (monitorBudgetGate.ts:141), while the monitor denies ingest-token fallback for reads in production by default (Usage-Monitor src/lib/ingest-auth.ts:48-60), so the gate can be silently inert (fails open with no alert). Ingest-path idempotency/DLQ robustness (question 5) matches the docs, with one nuance: the "up to 100 retries" DLQ budget reflects the Workers wrangler config; the production Deno durable queue uses maxAttempts=8 plus bounded dead-letter cycles (src/deno/durableQueue.ts:13), which is safe because the R2 outbox backstops everything.

gaps.title: Deno.cron-initiated work (incl. the entire new price chain) bypasses trackedFetch telemetry in production
gaps.detail: trackedFetch only emits when an AsyncLocalStorage context exists (thirdPartyTelemetry.ts:1048-1049,1062). withThirdPartyTelemetry is applied solely in the Workers-style fetch/scheduled/queue handlers (app/src/index.ts:328,341,425). So the daily-market-data lane (peer/Massive/Tiingo price refresh), hourly enrichment (the FMP 403 burn), watcher downloads, disclosure-latency probes, and durable-queue-drained extraction work likely produce ZERO request-attempt events in prod — contradicting third-party-usage-telemetry.md:3-7 ('reports every app-owned third-party HTTP attempt'). Only HTTP-triggered runs (e.g. POST /api/admin/backfill-market, runtime-tick) are metered, because Deno's HTTP server routes through the wrapped default export (src/deno/main.ts:232-235 → index.ts:547-551). EFFORT-LOG.md:943 confirms the internal lane crons are live on prod. Caveat: cannot verify CT_DISABLE_INTERNAL_CRON is unset in the Coolify env store; if an external scheduler drives runtime-tick instead, severity drops.
gaps.fixSketch: Wrap every Deno-side entry point in withThirdPartyTelemetry(env, ...): the Deno.cron tick callback in src/deno/main.ts (around runScheduledTick), runDailyLane in src/deno/cronLanes.ts (around lane.run), and (defensively) the drainDurableQueues invocation. Alternatively give trackedFetch a required env fallback path. Add a regression test mirroring the existing static raw-fetch scan that asserts Deno.cron registrations wrap the telemetry context, and verify post-deploy that provider=massive/tiingo/external-api events appear at ~00:07 UTC.

This contradicts third-party-usage-telemetry.md:84-86 ('peer... destinations use fixed provider categories'), mixes SocraticTrade traffic with any other unmapped host, and makes a monitor-side 'peer-app' provider budget row unmatchable. The outbound push path does it correctly (share/outbound.ts:128).

Keep service 'market-prices'/operations as-is so peer reads stay distinguishable from the push path. gaps.detail: CT ships success/status/rateLimited/errorType in event metadata (thirdPartyTelemetry.ts:1076-1083,1102-1111) and the receiver persists metadata (Usage-Monitor ingest route.ts:359), but no read surface exposes or aggregates it: the raw usage-events API selects everything except metadata (src/app/api/usage-events/route.ts:71-85) and budget-status has no error/rate-limit dimension (src/lib/budget-status.ts). So even when the ~283/day dead-FMP calls are delivered, an operator sees only cost-less fmp request counts — not that 100% are 403s. Combined with the cron-wrap gap above, the scheduled burn is likely fully invisible today.
gaps.fixSketch: Usage-Monitor: add error/rate-limit visibility — either include metadata in the raw usage-events response, or (better) aggregate per-provider counts of metadata.success=false / rateLimited=true / status buckets into the usage-events summary and provider detail pages, and optionally surface a 'failing provider' flag in /api/budget-status so producers can react.

gaps.title: Price chain has no monitor-informed pre-emptive throttle; budget-status cannot express request-rate quotas
gaps.detail: The budget read-back loop exists (monitorBudgetGate.ts, GET /api/budget-status, documented config-registry.md:148-168) but its only consumer is the extraction backlog autopilot (autopilot.ts:1036). runPriceRefresh (prices/service.ts:294-593) relies solely on local mechanisms: FMP daily cap + pacer, 429 retry/backoff, and fatal-abort classification. Nothing consults cross-app data before hitting the shared Massive key that sibling apps also saturate (the exact cause of the 2026-07-31 429 aborts). Additionally, /api/budget-status is monthly-USD only (BudgetStatusLevel/percentUsed, lib/budget-status.ts:76-165), so it structurally cannot represent Massive's per-minute limit or FMP's daily call cap — even a willing consumer has nothing to read.

gaps.title: Budget-gate read auth can be silently inert in production (ingest-token fallback denied by monitor)

The monitor denies the ingest-token fallback for reads in production unless USAGE_READ_TOKEN_ALLOW_INGEST_FALLBACK=true (Usage-Monitor src/lib/ingest-auth.ts:48-60), and 503s all bearer reads when USAGE_READ_TOKEN is unset (budget-status/route.ts:20-29). Code hardening (CT): in fetchBudgetStatusUncached, log-once (console.log, not Sentry) on persistent 401/503 responses so an inert gate is discoverable; optionally surface gate health in the admin connections panel next to the existing usage-telemetry fallback health.
